sentences: Meningitis is an inflammation of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, known as the meninges
This condition can be caused by various infectious agents, including bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites, as well as non-infectious causes such as certain medications and autoimmune diseases
Bacterial meningitis is often more severe and can lead to serious complications or death if not treated promptly
Common bacterial pathogens include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib)
Viral meningitis is generally less severe and often resolves without specific treatment
Common viral causes include enteroviruses, herpes simplex virus, and varicella-zoster virus
Symptoms of meningitis can include sudden onset of fever, headache, stiff neck, nausea, vomiting, increased sensitivity to light (photophobia), and altered mental status
Diagnosis typically involves clinical evaluation, lumbar puncture to analyze cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and laboratory tests to identify the causative agent
Treatment depends on the underlying cause
Bacterial meningitis requires prompt antibiotic therapy, while viral meningitis may only require supportive care
Vaccination is available for some types of bacterial meningitis and is an effective preventive measure

snippets.output: Meningitis is inflammation of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord, called the meninges.
Meningitis can be caused by bacterial, viral, fungal, parasitic agents, certain medications, or autoimmune diseases.
If untreated, bacterial meningitis may cause serious complications or death.
Common bacterial pathogens that cause meningitis include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Haemophilus influenzae type b.
Common viral causes of meningitis include enteroviruses, herpes simplex virus, and varicella‑zoster virus.
Typical symptoms of meningitis are fever, headache, stiff neck, nausea, vomiting, photophobia, and altered mental status.
Diagnosis of meningitis involves clinical evaluation, lumbar puncture to analyze cerebrospinal fluid, and laboratory tests to identify the causal agent.
Treatment of meningitis depends on its cause: bacterial meningitis requires prompt antibiotic therapy, whereas viral meningitis may only need supportive care.
Vaccinations targeting certain bacterial meningitis pathogens are available and effectively prevent those infections.
